content:
We need retrosynthesis of target: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

Structure: a tolyl sulfonamide attached to a phenyl ring bearing a trans-α,β-unsaturated amide attached to an aniline (anilide). So overall three fragments: tolyl sulfonyl chloride? Actually sulfonamide linking two aryl groups: tolyl-sulfonyl-aryl (para tolyl). The other aryl has a side chain: /C=C/C(=O)N-Ph-NH2 (anilide with an aniline at the amide nitrogen). So we can think disconnections:

1) Disconnection of sulfonamide: break S-N bond to give tolyl sulfonyl chloride (or sulfonyl fluoride) and aniline (aryl amine). So step: sulfonylation of aniline with tolyl sulfonyl chloride.

2) Disconnection of amide: break C(=O)-N bond to give carboxylic acid (or acid chloride) and aniline (the aniline attached to amide). So step: amide formation between aniline (the same as above? Actually the amide nitrogen is attached to phenyl ring (c3ccccc3N). That's an aniline (para? Actually it's an aniline with NH2). So we have aniline (aniline) reacting with cinnamic acid derivative (trans-α,β-unsaturated acid) to form amide.

But note the aniline is part of the same phenyl ring that also bears the sulfonamide? Wait the target: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We have two phenyl rings: ring A (tolyl) with sulfonamide attached to N. The sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to sulfonyl group which is attached to ring B (phenyl) that has the side chain (C=C-CO-N-Ph-NH2). So the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to sulfonyl group, not to aniline. So the sulfonamide nitrogen is part of the tolyl sulfonamide? Actually the SMILES: Cc1ccc(N S(=O)(=O) c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)N c3ccccc3N) cc2) cc1. So the N attached to tolyl is the sulfonamide nitrogen (connected to tolyl ring). The sulfonyl group attaches to ring B. So the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to tolyl ring (as an aniline) and to sulfonyl group. So the sulfonamide nitrogen is the same as the aniline of tolyl ring. So the sulfonamide formation is between tolyl amine (p-toluidine) and sulfonyl chloride derived from ring B (aryl sulfonyl chloride). So step 1: p-toluidine + aryl sulfonyl chloride (from ring B) -> target sulfonamide.

Now ring B also has side chain: /C=C/C(=O)N-Ph-NH2 attached at para position relative to sulfonyl? Actually the SMILES: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2 attached to sulfonyl group. So ring B is a phenyl sulfonyl attached to tolyl via sulfonamide. Ring B also has a para (or meta) substituent: trans-cinnamoyl anilide (with an aniline at the amide nitrogen). So we can further disconnect the amide: break C(=O)-N bond to give cinnamic acid (or acid chloride) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). So step 2: amide formation between aniline (aniline) and cinnamic acid (or acid chloride). The aniline is separate from the sulfonamide nitrogen; it's a different aniline (c3ccccc3N). So we need that aniline as a leaf.

Thus overall route: 2 steps (amide formation, sulfonamide formation). That's within 3 steps.

Now we need commercially available precursors: p-toluidine (4-methylaniline) is cheap. Aryl sulfonyl chloride: 4-(trans-cinnamoyl)phenylsulfonyl chloride? Actually we need sulfonyl chloride derived from ring B (phenyl sulfonyl chloride) that also has the side chain attached. So we need 4-(trans-cinnamoyl)benzenesulfonyl chloride (or 4-(cinnamoyl)benzenesulfonyl chloride). Is that commercially available? Might be. Could also use sulfonylation via sulfonyl chloride from sulfonic acid (benzenesulfonic acid) then chlorination. But we need to keep side chain intact. Likely 4-(cinnamoyl)benzenesulfonyl chloride is available.

Alternatively, we could first form the amide on the phenyl ring, then sulfonylate with tolyl sulfonyl chloride (p-toluenesulfonyl chloride) to attach to the other ring. But the sulfonyl group is attached to ring B, not to tolyl. So we could use p-toluenesulfonyl chloride (TsCl) reacting with aniline (the tolyl amine) to give p-tolyl sulfonamide attached to the aniline (which is the same as target). But the sulfonyl group would be p-tolyl, not the aryl with side chain. So not correct.

Thus we need aryl sulfonyl chloride with side chain. Could be commercially available as 4-(cinnamoyl)benzenesulfonyl chloride. Let's check availability via search_catalog_by_smiles.
